contract.one_registry: This file is the canonical launcher registry. The PWA launcher (apps.js), the native shell (app_registry.json) and the HTTP bridge all serve the SAME app set; verify-app-registry.py fails on any drift between them.
contract.capability_source: services/nuxel-bridge/src/capabilities.py (Capability enum) — an app may not declare a capability the bridge does not know.
contract.manifest_rule: every pwa entry must resolve to a real index.html AND a manifest.json carrying nuxel.capabilities (list) and nuxel.bridge_version equal to the pin.

capability_gaps.note: The apps ask for a read/write storage pair; the bridge enum defines storage:persistent only. Not fatal for the registry (the ids are a manifest contract, not an enforcement claim) but an app must not advertise a capability the host cannot arbitrate - the owning group either adds the enum entry or moves the manifests to storage:persistent.

The Terminal's PTY is opened by the native PWA host (tools/s10plus/a3x/nuxel-pwa-host.c), NOT through the bridge capability model, so no bridge enum entry exists. Recorded so the gap is visible instead of implied.

launcher_manifest_notes: pwa/nuxel-home/manifest.json (owned by the Priority 2 group) declares nuxel.bridge_version 0.5.2-beta, which is the HOST version, not the protocol pin '1'. Reported as a WARN by the verifier: the launcher is a system surface, not a third-party app, so it is not part of apps[] and the mismatch cannot reject a PWA, but the two fields should not be conflated.

required_apps_not_yet_in_tree.note: Per-app permission states, global kill switches, kernel-confinement reality (Linux 4.14: no Landlock). No tree path is claimed here on purpose: this is the concept-level inventory, and a path guess would make the verifier report a directory that will not exist.
One authoritative backend (firewalld or UFW), blocklists, hosts editor with atomic writes.
OpenVPN/WireGuard profiles via NetworkManager, Tor SOCKS control, SSH/SFTP/VNC/SMB clients.
Read-only audit with recorded coverage/version; never presented as a certified CIS score.
CPU/memory/storage/thermal/sensor readouts plus the hardware capability inventory.

notes.tree_apps_states: complete | in_progress | shared-assets-not-an-app (the dir MUST exist) | planned (must NOT exist yet; DEFER until it lands). Enforced by tools/s10plus/a33/verify-app-registry.py - a dangling directory in a present-state entry is a FAILED verdict, never a warning.
notes.registry_version_stays_4: tree_apps/required_apps_not_yet_in_tree are INVENTORY sections: they do not change apps[] or its urls, so NUXEL_REGISTRY_VERSION in pwa/nuxel-home/js/apps.js (owned by the Priority 2 group) must NOT be bumped by this revision. verify-app-registry.py fails on any registry_version drift.
notes.required_apps_not_yet_in_tree: Concept-level inventory of mission-required apps with no tree directory yet. Each entry names the owning build group and its ledger briq; the verifier fails if that briq file does not exist in docs/beta-finalization/workqueue/ or if the briq's component does not match owner_group.
